verdict.rationale: Datadog's own Experiments feature documents creating and versioning datasets and comparing results. Its SDKs and evaluations API let code submit evaluations, so the core of the story exists in the product. However, the evidence never shows an agent programmatically creating a dataset, triggering an experiment/eval run, or reading results back through the API or SDK. Submitting external evaluations is not the same as triggering an eval run. Missing for 10: documented programmatic dataset-creation API/SDK calls, a documented way to trigger an experiment or eval run from code, a documented API to read back results, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create a dataset, trigger an eval run programmatically, and read back the results

citations.quote: It helps you understand how changes to prompts, models, providers, or system architecture affect performance.
You can use the evaluations API provided by Agent Observability to send evaluations associated with spans, traces, or sessions to Datadog.
